pos.personaBrief: Sacchi's Milan pressed high to win the ball back and attacked in waves (StatsBomb: opened 10 shots before Steaua had one); the team wanted the ball and controlled the game, not ceding it to counter.

pro.personaBrief: Build-up started with the back four carrying the ball (Coaches' Voice), but the team was relatively direct via Gullit and 15 of 27 efforts came right after winning the ball high (StatsBomb).

est.personaBrief: A rigidly drilled 4-4-2 with compact lines and defined relationships, yet midfielders and forwards moved constantly and Donadoni and Ancelotti drifted between wide and central areas.

lar.personaBrief: Flanks were essential to Sacchi's offence (Coaches' Voice) but via advancing full-backs and hard-working wide midfielders, not classic dribbling wingers; stars like Gullit and Rijkaard played centrally.

blo.personaBrief: The defining feature: highest average defensive action of the competition, forwards pressing centre-backs, offside line as the first step of recovery (StatsBomb, Coaches' Voice).

mar.personaBrief: Pure zonal marking with no libero and Baresi as proactive defender (SempreMilan, Coaches' Voice); a block marking spaces and pressing the ball.

pla.personaBrief: Sacchi imposed his model through exhausting drills and was maniacal about his system (Van Basten); the team played the same way against all opponents.

res.personaBrief: Berlusconi wanted to win and convince through spectacular play and Sacchi promoted active, protagonist football; the team kept attacking (4-0 final) rather than shutting games.

sis.personaBrief: The collective system came first, everyone including Gullit and Van Basten pressed and did tactical duties; drilled movements turned a group into immortals.

jog.personaBrief: Technically gifted, intelligent players (Rijkaard, Ancelotti, Baresi) with high work rate; compactness made pressing less physically demanding, and the game was won by positioning not duels.

bas.personaBrief: Squad built through signings of Gullit, Van Basten, Rijkaard, Ancelotti and Parma/Udinese players in their prime; not an academy project, and prime-age players over proven veterans.

lid.personaBrief: Sacchi was the boss with total control of the model, maniacal and demanding in exhausting training, though Van Basten called him soft with stars; rules for the system came first.
